gaps.evidence: Built under ADM-09, taken by delegation: the inbound webhook already speaks WhatsApp Cloud API, so outbound over the same Graph API adds no vendor. crm.send_outbound_message records the message BEFORE the provider is called - a message sent and not recorded is invisible, a message recorded and not sent is visibly wrong - allocating seq under the conversation's lock and deduplicating on the caller's idempotency key. The number and the sending account are read from the database, so one organization cannot send as another. What the provider says is written back by crm.mark_outbound_delivery, which audits from inside its own transaction and refuses to re-settle a message. Inert without WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN, and it says so rather than appearing to work.

gaps.evidence: qa.defects carries what directive 19 asks of every bug: severity, reproduction (required - a bug nobody can reproduce is a rumour), expected, actual, environment, evidence, assignee, status, resolution and verification. ARCHITECTURE.md 4.8's vocabulary is kept as written. The gate it states is enforced inside projects.submit_deliverable, under the same lock that writes the status. Scoped to the version and to project-wide defects rather than to the project: a blocker on v1 must not stop v2, because v2 is the fix, and the project-wide reading would make the fix unshowable and reward closing bugs dishonestly.

gaps.title: Production-ready gate
Handover
gaps.evidence: projects.handovers and projects.handover_items record what was delivered, when, and whether the client said they had it. Directive 22's credentials rule shaped the schema: a credential item is incapable of holding a credential - reference must be null and transfer_method must say how it actually reached the client, refused in DDL rather than by a service that could forget. Delivery refuses an empty package and refuses while an open blocker or major defect stands (ARCHITECTURE.md 4.8, directive 20). The outstanding balance is reported and NOT gated on, because which payment is final is the project's own plan and inventing that rule would put a made-up gate in front of real revenue. Acceptance is the client's, through the approval engine, which gains 'handover' as a subject type.

gaps.evidence: Built as ARCHITECTURE.md 4.6 designs it, under ADM-08. approvals.approval_requests serves all eight subject types and both audiences; approvals.approval_policies holds who must decide, as owner-editable data with a money floor in DDL. The required role is snapshotted onto each request so a policy edited mid-flight cannot change the rule a pending request was raised under. Raising is idempotent through a partial unique index; deciding takes a row lock and a compare-and-swap; the tables accept no direct writes at all, so a role can never settle through PostgREST what the function would have refused. Every request and decision is audited from inside its own transaction.

gaps.evidence: Built: /approvals lists everything pending for the caller's organization, soonest deadline first, marking anything past its SLA. Approve, request changes and reject are one form each; a client-audience request also asks where the client agreed, because the database requires it. The page runs no role check of its own - what an approver may settle is decided under a lock against the role snapshotted on the request, so the button is drawn for everyone who can see the row and the refusal is surfaced as written. Overdue rows say plainly that nobody is notified, because escalation is G-096.

gaps.testCoverage: scripts/check-record.mjs, run by `npm run check` and by CI on every pull request. Proved red first: four planted disagreements, four failures, exit 1.
gaps.evidence: Closed. The claim of regeneration is replaced by a check that re-derives every number: gap totals from the gap records, the §4.8 tables and the README's gap count from those totals, the baseline's migrations, tables, RLS coverage, test files and live scripts from the filesystem, and the test counts from an actual run. It also fails if either copy carries a gap or decision id the other does not - the drift that hid G-078 and ADM-27 through ADM-37. What it does not do is write the documents; it refuses to let them disagree, which is the cheaper half and the half that was missing.

gaps.title: the unsupported snapshot is still a runnable script
gaps.testCoverage: None - the marking is checked, the runnability is not
gaps.evidence: ADM-40 kept supabase/_bundle.sql as a marked historical snapshot. The marking is prose, and prose does not stop a paste: the file still begins a transaction and still builds a schema missing D16, D17-D22, G-079, G-082, G-083 and G-084. One line - `do $$ begin raise exception '...' end $$;` before the begin - would make it refuse rather than merely warn, at the cost of the file no longer being runnable even deliberately. That trade was not part of the decision that was taken, so it is recorded rather than assumed.

gaps.title: nothing expires an unanswered approval request
gaps.testCoverage: tests/approval-engine.test.ts F - fails if an expiry function lands while this gap is still open
gaps.evidence: ADM-08c decided that an unanswered request expires and escalates to the owner, and is never auto-approved. The schema carries sla_due_at, the expired state and escalated_from; no job walks them, so an overdue request stays pending and visible rather than escalating. Shipping an unused expire function would have been the G-082 trap, so the gap is recorded instead. Closing it is a job kind, a handler and the escalation raise - and it needs ADM-39, which asks how long a client who has paid in full may wait.

gaps.title: a new schema is unreachable until PostgREST is told about it
gaps.testCoverage: scripts/verify-approvals.mjs - every check answered 406 PGRST106 until this was handled
gaps.evidence: Found by running the live verification rather than by reasoning. PostgREST exposes the schemas named in pgrst.db_schemas on the authenticator role - what the dashboard's Exposed schemas setting writes - and a migration that creates a schema does not appear there. 20260812120011 now appends itself to that list, idempotently and additively, and warns rather than fails if it lacks the grant. What is still open is the general case: the next schema will hit this again, and nothing checks that every schema a module reads is exposed.

gaps.title: a Server Action could not be executed by a test, only read
gaps.testCoverage: tests/approval-centre.test.ts - twelve behavioural tests over an action module
gaps.evidence: next/cache does not resolve outside a Next build, so importing any 'use server' module from the test runner failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Action tests therefore asserted on source text - structural assertions standing in for behaviour, which directive 38 permits only as a supplement. tests/_alias.mjs now maps next/cache to an inert stub, so an action is an ordinary module of async functions again and its outcome mapping can be driven for real. The existing source-text assertions in requirement-proposal.test.ts are left alone; they can be rewritten when that area is next touched.

gaps.title: a dead job cannot be requeued from anywhere
gaps.evidence: /operations shows what the system gave up on; nothing brings it back. Reviving a dead unlock or extraction is a write with real consequences - a duplicate invoice, a second milestone opened - so it needs an idempotency story rather than a button. Recorded rather than added to a page whose job is to tell the truth.

gaps.title: an approved deliverable gates nothing
gaps.evidence: A design or prototype can now be approved by the client and the approval changes nothing else: no milestone unlocks, no invoice is released, no project status moves. Which approvals gate which payments is a business rule - ADM-13 and ADM-14 - and wiring one before the rule is written would put the wrong gate in front of real money. The record is built; the gates wait for the rules.

adminDecisions.title: How long may a client who has paid in full wait for the next stage to open before somebody is told?
adminDecisions.why: D18 gave the retry ladder ~19 minutes of real spacing. After that the job is dead and nothing tries again. The ladder is an engineering default; the number is a business rule nobody has stated. DELEGATED: One hour, matching the alert cooldown already shipped. Taken by delegation 2026-08-13; a number nobody had stated, chosen so the ladder can exist, and cheap to change.

adminDecisions.title: Is supabase/_bundle.sql a supported install path?
adminDecisions.why: It is twelve migrations stale and ships the D19 defect. Either CI regenerates it on every migration, or it is deleted and `db push` is documented as the only way in. Keeping it as-is means the documented install produces a knowingly defective deployment. Granted 2026-08-12: keep it, marked unsupported. Neither regenerated in CI nor deleted - the header now says what it is and what it is missing, and check-record.mjs pins the marking. Residual recorded as G-095.

adminDecisions.title: Does winning a deal qualify its lead, or must a lead be qualified before a deal can be won?
adminDecisions.why: Nothing requires a lead to be qualified before a deal is opened on it, so the ordinary path is new -> deal won -> converted. LEAD_TRANSITIONS says only qualified may become converted. Both cannot be true. D20 preserved today's behaviour rather than pick.

adminDecisions.title: When a past client comes back, is that a new deal on the same lead, or a new lead?
adminDecisions.why: WhatsApp ingest keys a lead to a phone number permanently, so a returning client lands on the same lead row. D21 stopped the schema from forbidding a second deal there, but createOpportunity still returns the settled one instead of raising a new one. Which behaviour is right is a sales-process question.

adminDecisions.title: Who may change a deal's value after it is opened, and is a change of price audited?
adminDecisions.why: value_minor is written at insert and never updated, and convertToProject seeds the project budget from it. A reopened deal re-won at a different figure converts into a project budgeted at the old one.
